This was the idea of Thiel, who thought "venture capital is due for a slimdown", which caused some resistance from inside the firm.{{cite news |last1=Primack |first1=Dan |last2=Kokalitcheva |first2=Kia |title=Scoop: Founders Fund slashes size of its flagship VC fund |url=https://www.axios.com/2023/03/03/founders-fund-slashes-vc-peter-thiel |date=3 March 2023}}{{Cite web |title=Founders Fund |url=https://angelspartners.com/firm/founders-fund |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240804205757/https://angelspartners.com/firm/founders-fund |archive-date=August 4, 2024 |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=Angels Partners}} In 2025, Founders Fund raised its third growth fund, Founders Fund Growth III, at $4.6 billion for late-stage investments.{{Cite web |last=Prabhu |first=Abhinaya |date=2025-04-16 |title=Peter Thiel's Founders Fund reloaded: $4.6B to fuel the next wave of tech titans — TFN |url=https://techfundingnews.com/peter-thiels-founders-fund-reloaded-4-6b-to-fuel-the-next-wave-of-tech-titans/ |access-date=2025-04-23 |website=Tech Funding News |language=en}} Julie Bort of ''[[TechCrunch]]'' remarks that, "Founders Fund is so big and successful that it can always raise an oversubscribed fund should it choose to." The over-subscription seemed to anticipate an era of big VC spending, and also expansion of the defense sector. Meanwhile, ''[[CNBC]]'' commented that, "Hefty amounts of private capital are likely to be needed for the foreseeable future as the IPO market remains virtually dormant".{{cite news |last1=Levy |first1=Ari |title=Peter Thiel's Founders Fund closes $4.6 billion growth fund |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/04/11/peter-thiels-founders-fund-closes-4point6-billion-growth-fund.html |work=CNBC |date=11 April 2025 |language=en}} ==Philosophy and development== [[File:Trae Stephens of Founders Fund at 2024 TechCrunch StrictlyVC event.jpg|thumb|[[Trae Stephens]] at 2024 TechCrunch StrictlyVC event]] The Founders Fund was conceptualized as an early-stage venture capital fund. From the start, it has adopted Thiel's contrarian attitude, and bet early and aggressively on companies with the founders it deemed deserving of trust. Early in its history, it made many investments in internet or social media and health and life science research, among which there were investments in [[Spotify]], [[Airbnb]], and [[Lyft]].{{cite news |title=Life After Facebook |url=https://www.forbes.com/forbes/2011/0214/features-peter-thiel-social-media-life-after-facebook.html |work=Forbes |date=26 January 2011 |language=en}}{{cite web |last1=O'Dea |first1=Meghan |title=German Historical Institute Washington Bulletin, Supplement Bd. 12 (2016) |url=https://perspectivia.net/servlets/MCRFileNodeServlet/ploneimport_derivate_00000228/333.pdf |access-date=21 October 2025}} By 2006, Jessica Guynn of ''[[SFGate]]'' characterized it as a tiny but influential fund focusing on consumer internet, standing beside Thiel's then extraordinarily successful firm [[Clarium Capital]].{{cite news |last1=Guynn |first1=Jessica |title=The Founders Fund emerges as venture capital 2.0 / How entrepreneurs get money, and time, for startups is changing |url=https://www.sfgate.com/bayarea/article/The-Founders-Fund-emerges-as-venture-capital-2-0-2543274.php |access-date=21 October 2025 |date=13 December 2006}} Later, together with Thiel's disillusion with social media companies, the firm has gradually developed into a primary backer of [[hard tech]] and defense technology. In 2011, when the social bubble was still expanding, he complained, "Is [[Twitter]] worth $7 billion?" At this time, the Founders Fund had developed a portfolio in artificial intelligence, biotech and space technology. In 2017, it published the manifesto "What happened to the future?", written by [[Bruce Gibney]]. The manifesto denied that the Internet's potential had been exhausted, but emphasized that the Founders' Fund would focus on ambitious projects that resolved real challenges. Other than these companies and [[SpaceX]], the Founders Fund makes investments in other notable companies or projects that have strategical value for defense, security or government affairs, including: {{Quote box |quote = Miles Kruppa revealed that Founders Fund was sitting on a more than $19.5 billion gain from its investment in SpaceX since it started investing in 2008—more than its total assets under management! Founders Fund is an American venture capital fund founded in 2005 based in San Francisco. The fund has roughly $17 billion in total assets under management as of 2025. The firm was founded by Peter Thiel, Ken Howery, and Luke Nosek.
Founders Fund was the first institutional investor in Space Exploration Technologies (SpaceX) and Palantir Technologies, and an early investor in Facebook. The firm's partners have been founders, early employees and investors at companies including PayPal, Palantir Technologies, Anduril Industries and SpaceX. The firm's investments include Airbnb, Anduril, DeepMind, Rippling, Facebook, Ramp, Palantir Technologies, Polymarket, Pudgy Penguins, SpaceX, Spotify, Stripe, Neuralink, and Nubank.
Notable partners include Peter Thiel, Trae Stephens, and Mike Solana. Former partners include Brian Singerman, Keith Rabois, Cyan Banister, Ken Howery, Kevin Hartz, Sean Parker, and Bruce Gibney.
